note: R25-eb: fresh untouched set, written without access to tests or other question sets

stories.text: Every Saturday morning, Mrs. Okafor opened her small bakery on Elm Street at six o'clock. Her son Chidi helped her carry the trays of warm bread to the front window. One rainy Saturday, the oven stopped working because a fuse had blown. Chidi ran to the hardware store next door and bought a new fuse for three dollars. By eight o'clock the shop smelled of fresh loaves again, and the first customer was a tired mail carrier named Paul.
qs: Why did the oven stop working?
How much did the new fuse cost?
a tired mail carrier named paul

stories.text: Kenji Watanabe noticed that his grey cat, Mochi, had not come home for dinner. He searched the garden, the garage and the narrow alley behind the house. At nine in the evening, his neighbour Mrs. Ito knocked on the door holding a shoebox. Inside the box was Mochi, who had fallen asleep in her laundry basket. Kenji thanked her with a jar of homemade plum jam.
qs: What was the name of Kenji's cat?
When did Mrs. Ito knock on the door?
How did Kenji thank Mrs. Ito?
with a jar of homemade plum jam
a jar of homemade plum jam

stories.text: Dr. Anjali Patel rode her blue bicycle to the clinic because her car had a flat tyre. On the way, she stopped at a cafe to buy a cup of masala tea. A young boy named Arjun was crying on the bench outside because he had scraped his knee. Dr. Patel cleaned the cut with water from her bottle and covered it with a plaster. She arrived at the clinic ten minutes late, but nobody minded.
qs: How did Dr. Patel get to the clinic?
Why didn't Dr. Patel drive her car?
because her car had a flat tyre
her car had a flat tyre
What did she buy at the cafe?
because he had scraped his knee
How late did she arrive at the clinic?

stories.text: Lars and his grandfather Olav rowed a wooden boat across the lake before sunrise. They had brought two fishing rods, a flask of coffee and a bag of worms. For three hours they caught nothing at all. Just as they were about to leave, Olav's line pulled hard, and he reeled in a huge trout. Lars took a photograph of the fish, and then they let it swim away.
qs: Who rowed the boat with Lars?
When did they row across the lake?
How many fishing rods had they brought?
What kind of fish did Olav catch?
What did they do with the fish after the photograph?

stories.text: Amara had practised her lines for the school play every night for two weeks. She was playing the queen, and her costume was a long purple dress with a paper crown. On the night of the show, she forgot her first line and froze on the stage. Her best friend Zainab whispered the words from behind the curtain. Amara finished the play perfectly, and the audience clapped for a full minute.
qs: How long had Amara practised her lines?
What was her crown made of?
Who whispered the words to Amara?
How long did the audience clap?

stories.text: Mr. Hernandez grew tomatoes, peppers and beans in the garden behind his apartment building. In July, he noticed that something was eating his ripe tomatoes at night. He set up a small camera on the fence to find the thief. The next morning, the video showed a raccoon climbing over the wall with a tomato in its mouth. Mr. Hernandez laughed and built a wire cage around the plants.
qs: When did he notice something eating his tomatoes?
Where did he set up the camera?
Which animal was eating the tomatoes?
What did he build around the plants?

stories.text: Fatima took the early train from Leeds to London to attend a job interview. She had printed her CV twice in case one copy got wet. Halfway through the journey, the train stopped for forty minutes because of a signal problem. Fatima phoned the company, and the manager, Mr. Clarke, agreed to meet her at noon instead. She got the job and started work the following Monday.
qs: How long did the train stop?
Who agreed to meet her at noon?

stories.text: Biscuit was a small brown dog who belonged to the Mensah family. Every Sunday, Kofi Mensah took him to the beach to chase the waves. One Sunday, Biscuit dug in the sand and found an old silver watch. Kofi handed the watch to the lifeguard, who put a notice on the board by the car park. Two days later, an elderly man named Mr. Boateng came to collect it and gave Biscuit a bone.
qs: How often did Kofi take Biscuit to the beach?
What did Biscuit find in the sand?
Who did Kofi hand the watch to?
What did Mr. Boateng give Biscuit?

stories.text: Ms. Novak worked at the town library, where she ran a reading club for children on Wednesday afternoons. This week, only three children came because of the heavy snow. Instead of reading quietly, they built a fort out of cushions and read ghost stories inside it with a torch. Little Tomas was so scared by one story that he hid under a blanket. Ms. Novak promised to choose a funny book next time.
qs: When did the reading club meet?
How many children came this week?
What did they build the fort out of?
Why did Tomas hide under a blanket?
was so scared by one story

stories.text: Grandma Lin went to the morning market with a woven basket and a list written on the back of an envelope. She bought six eggs, a bunch of spring onions and a fresh fish from her old friend Mr. Wong. When she reached for her purse, she realised she had left it at home. Mr. Wong told her not to worry and said she could pay him tomorrow. On the way back, Grandma Lin bought him a bag of lychees with the coins in her pocket.
qs: What did Grandma Lin carry to the market?
on the back of an envelope
How many eggs did she buy?
What had she left at home?
What did she buy for Mr. Wong?

stories.text: Diego was the goalkeeper for the Riverside Under-12 football team. In the final match of the season, the score was tied at one goal each with five minutes left. The other team won a penalty after a foul near the goal. Diego dived to his left and stopped the ball with his fingertips. His coach, Mrs. Alvarez, lifted him onto her shoulders after the final whistle.
qs: What was the score with five minutes left?
Why did the other team win a penalty?
after a foul near the goal
How did Diego stop the ball?
dived to his left and stopped the ball with his fingertips

stories.text: The Rossi family moved into a yellow house at the end of Maple Lane in late August. Sofia, who was nine, chose the small bedroom with a round window. While unpacking, her father dropped a box of plates, and four of them broke. Their new neighbours, the Kowalskis, brought over a lasagne and a set of spare plates that evening. Sofia decided that Maple Lane was going to be a good place to live.
qs: When did the Rossi family move?
the small bedroom with a round window

stories.text: Mrs. Adeyemi kept a green parrot called Captain in a cage near her kitchen window. Captain could say hello, goodbye and the name of the postman, Ben. One afternoon, Mrs. Adeyemi left the cage door open while she cleaned it, and Captain flew out into the street. After an hour of searching, she heard someone shouting 'Ben! Ben!' from the top of an oak tree. She held up a slice of apple, and Captain flew straight down to her arm.
qs: Why did Captain fly out into the street?
mrs. adeyemi left the cage door open
from the top of an oak tree
the top of an oak tree
What did she use to bring Captain down?

stories.text: Priya and Hassan were getting married on a sunny Saturday in May. Hassan's aunt Leila had baked a three-layer cake decorated with white roses. While the van was driving to the hall, it hit a pothole and the top layer slid sideways. Leila fixed the cake in the car park with a spoon and a tub of icing. None of the guests noticed, and the couple cut the cake at four o'clock.
qs: How many layers did the cake have?
What happened when the van hit a pothole?
Where did Leila fix the cake?
When did the couple cut the cake?

stories.text: During the worst snowstorm of the winter, the power went out in Mr. Lindqvist's village. He lit four candles and made soup on his old wood stove. His neighbour Astrid, who lived alone, had no stove of her own, so he invited her over. They played cards by candlelight until the lights came back on at midnight. Astrid won every game except the last one.
qs: When did the power go out?
during the worst snowstorm of the winter
How many candles did Mr. Lindqvist light?
What did he make the soup on?
Why did he invite Astrid over?
had no stove of her own
Who won most of the card games?

stories.text: Mr. Kamau drove the number 14 bus through the city centre every weekday. On Tuesday, a woman left a violin case on the back seat and got off at the museum stop. Mr. Kamau noticed it at the end of the route and took it to the lost property office. The next morning, the woman, a music teacher named Ms. Duarte, was waiting at the bus stop to thank him. She played a short song for the passengers before the bus pulled away.
qs: Which bus did Mr. Kamau drive?
What did the woman leave on the back seat?
Where did the woman get off?
Where did Mr. Kamau take the case?

stories.text: Noa and her brother Eli went camping in the hills with their parents. They put up a green tent beside a stream and collected sticks for a fire. That night, they heard strange scratching outside the tent. Eli shone his torch through the gap and saw a hedgehog eating crumbs from their plates. In the morning, Noa drew a picture of the hedgehog in her notebook.
qs: Where did they put up the tent?
What did they hear that night?
Who drew a picture of the hedgehog?

stories.text: Mr. Haddad had run a tailor's shop on Station Road for thirty years. One Friday, a nervous young man named Omar brought in a suit that was far too long in the sleeves. Omar needed it for his sister's graduation the next day. Mr. Haddad stayed late and shortened the sleeves by five centimetres. When Omar collected the suit on Saturday morning, it fitted perfectly.
qs: How long had Mr. Haddad run his shop?
What was wrong with Omar's suit?
far too long in the sleeves
Why did Omar need the suit?
By how much did Mr. Haddad shorten the sleeves?
When did Omar collect the suit?

stories.text: Aunt Marisol kept three beehives at the bottom of her orchard. Each autumn, her niece Lucia came to help collect the honey. They wore white suits and gloves, and Marisol used a smoker to calm the bees. This year, Lucia was stung once on the wrist when a bee crawled into her sleeve. They filled twenty jars, and Lucia took four of them home to her parents.
qs: How many beehives did Aunt Marisol keep?
at the bottom of her orchard
Why did Marisol use a smoker?
How many jars did Lucia take home?

stories.text: Mei woke up late on the morning of her maths exam because her alarm clock battery had died. She had no time for breakfast, so she grabbed a banana and ran to the bus stop. Her friend Ravi saved her a seat at the front of the exam hall. The hardest question was about the area of a triangle, but Mei remembered the formula. Two weeks later, she learned that she had scored ninety-two percent.
qs: Why did Mei wake up late?
because her alarm clock battery had died
her alarm clock battery had died
What did she grab for breakfast?
What was the hardest question about?

stories.text: Chef Dubois was preparing dinner for a party of twelve when the delivery of fresh fish failed to arrive. He looked in the cold room and found chicken, mushrooms and a large bag of rice. Quickly, he changed the menu to chicken with mushroom sauce. His assistant, Yuki, made a lemon tart for dessert. The guests said it was the best meal they had eaten all year.
qs: How many people was the dinner for?
Where did the chef look for other food?

stories.text: For Grandpa Ivan's eightieth birthday, his granddaughter Nadia repaired his old wall clock. The clock had stopped working ten years earlier, and Ivan had kept it in the attic. Nadia found a clockmaker in the next town who sold her a new spring. She spent three evenings cleaning the gears with a soft brush. When Ivan heard it chime again at the party, he wiped tears from his eyes.
qs: Which birthday was Grandpa Ivan celebrating?
Where had Ivan kept the clock?
Who sold Nadia a new spring?
a clockmaker in the next town
How many evenings did Nadia spend cleaning the gears?
What did she clean the gears with?

stories.text: On a windy afternoon in March, Ahmed flew his red kite in the park near the river. A strong gust snapped the string, and the kite floated over the water. It landed in the branches of a willow tree on the far bank. A park keeper named Mrs. Greene fetched a long ladder from her shed. She climbed up, untangled the kite, and gave it back to Ahmed with a new roll of string.
qs: When did Ahmed fly his kite?
on a windy afternoon in march
in the branches of a willow tree
What did Mrs. Greene fetch from her shed?

stories.text: Ms. Nakamura asked her art class to paint something that made them happy. Leo painted his grandmother's kitchen, and Ama painted a field of sunflowers. Ben could not decide, so he painted a picture of his own empty page. Ms. Nakamura laughed and hung all twenty-two paintings in the school corridor. Parents came to see the display on Thursday evening.
qs: What did Ms. Nakamura ask the class to paint?
Why did Ben paint his own empty page?

stories.text: Jack and his wife Mia were driving across the desert to visit her brother in Alice Springs. About fifty kilometres from the town, their car got a flat tyre. Jack discovered that the spare tyre was also flat. A truck driver named Bruce stopped and lent them his pump. They reached Alice Springs just after sunset, hot and dusty but laughing.
qs: Who were Jack and Mia going to visit?
How far from the town did they get a flat tyre?
When did they reach Alice Springs?

stories.text: Mrs. Mbeki led the church choir in her small town every Thursday evening. The choir was preparing to sing at the mayor's Christmas concert. Two weeks before the concert, the lead singer, Thabo, lost his voice because of a bad cold. A shy teenager named Lindiwe offered to sing his part. At the concert, her clear voice surprised everyone, and the mayor asked her to sing again next year.
qs: Where was the choir preparing to sing?
Why did Thabo lose his voice?
Who offered to sing Thabo's part?
What did the mayor ask Lindiwe to do?

stories.text: Mr. O'Brien's old horse, Daisy, escaped from her field one foggy morning. She had pushed open the gate, which someone had forgotten to latch. Mr. O'Brien and his daughter Siobhan followed her hoofprints along the muddy lane. They found Daisy in the schoolyard, eating the grass beside the swings. The children cheered when Siobhan led her home on a rope.
qs: she had pushed open the gate
What did they follow along the lane?
How did Siobhan lead Daisy home?

stories.text: Dr. Wei Chen left her phone in a taxi after a long night shift at the hospital. She borrowed a colleague's phone and called her own number. The taxi driver, Mr. Singh, answered and said he was already across the city. He promised to drop it off at the hospital reception at the end of his shift. At seven the next morning, the phone was waiting for her in an envelope with her name on it.
qs: Where did Dr. Chen leave her phone?
Where had she worked the night shift?
When was the phone waiting for her?

stories.text: The pupils of Hillside Primary School decided to clean up the riverbank for their science project. Their teacher, Mr. Abara, gave each of them a pair of gloves and a rubbish bag. In two hours, they collected forty bags of rubbish, including an old bicycle wheel and a shopping trolley. A reporter from the local newspaper took a photo of the class. The next week, the town council put new bins along the river.
qs: Which school did the pupils attend?
What did Mr. Abara give each pupil?
a pair of gloves and a rubbish bag
How many bags of rubbish did they collect?
Who took a photo of the class?
a reporter from the local newspaper
What did the town council do the next week?
put new bins along the river

stories.text: Ana wanted to make her grandmother's famous dumplings for the New Year's party. Her grandmother, Zofia, lived in Krakow, so Ana called her on a video call. Zofia explained every step slowly while Ana kneaded the dough in her kitchen in Chicago. The first batch fell apart in the boiling water because the dough was too thin. The second batch was perfect, and Ana saved one on a plate to show her grandmother.
qs: What did Ana want to make?
How did Ana contact her grandmother?
Why did the first batch fall apart?
because the dough was too thin

stories.text: Mr. Mendes was the last keeper of the lighthouse on Gull Island. Every evening at dusk, he climbed one hundred and twelve steps to switch on the great lamp. One stormy night, he spotted a small fishing boat drifting towards the rocks. He flashed the light three times and called the coastguard on his radio. The two fishermen on board were rescued and later visited him with a basket of sardines.
qs: How many steps did Mr. Mendes climb?
What did he spot one stormy night?
a small fishing boat drifting towards the rocks
Whom did he call on his radio?
What did the fishermen bring him?

stories.text: Kwame had entered the regional spelling bee after winning the contest at his school. On the day, he wore his lucky blue tie, which had belonged to his late grandfather. He spelled 'rhythm' and 'necessary' correctly, but he missed the word 'occasion' in the fourth round. He finished in third place out of thirty students. His mother took him for ice cream and told him she had never been prouder.
qs: In which round did he miss it?
What place did Kwame finish in?

stories.text: Every winter, the pond behind Pierre's farm froze solid enough for skating. Pierre tested the ice with an axe before letting anyone on it. On the first Saturday of January, twenty people from the village came with skates and thermos flasks. Elena, who had never skated before, held onto a kitchen chair to keep her balance. By the end of the day, she could skate a whole circle without the chair.
qs: How did Pierre test the ice?
When did the villagers come to skate?
on the first saturday of january
How many people came from the village?

stories.text: A ginger cat named Marmalade lived in Mrs. Fitzgerald's second-hand bookshop. He slept on the poetry shelf in the morning and in the shop window in the afternoon. Customers often bought a book just to have an excuse to stroke him. One day a tourist from Brazil, Gabriela, asked if the cat was for sale. Mrs. Fitzgerald smiled and said that Marmalade was the only thing in the shop that was not.
qs: What kind of shop did Mrs. Fitzgerald own?
Where did Marmalade sleep in the morning?
Why did customers often buy a book?
to have an excuse to stroke him

stories.text: Rahul was flying home to Mumbai after a year of studying in Toronto. At the airport, he found that his suitcase was four kilograms too heavy. He opened it on the floor and put on two jumpers and his winter coat. The check-in clerk, Ms. Brooks, laughed and said she had seen worse. Rahul sweated through the whole security line, but his bag was accepted.
qs: How long had he been studying in Toronto?
How much too heavy was his suitcase?
two jumpers and his winter coat

stories.text: In the village of Tamba, the only well dried up during a long, hot summer. Aisha and the other girls had to walk two hours each day to fetch water from the river. The village elders asked an engineer named Dr. Sow to help. He brought a team that dug a new, deeper well beside the school in three weeks. On the day the water came up, the whole village held a feast with music and dancing.
qs: When did the well dry up?
How long did Aisha walk each day?
Where was the new well dug?
How long did it take to dig the new well?

stories.text: Mrs. Rosenberg gave piano lessons in her living room every afternoon after school. Her youngest student, a six-year-old boy named Felix, could not reach the pedals. She stacked three thick cookbooks under his feet so that he could rest them. Felix practised a simple waltz for a month and played it at the spring recital. Afterwards, he asked if he could take the cookbooks home as a souvenir.
qs: Where did Mrs. Rosenberg give piano lessons?
Why did she stack cookbooks under his feet?
What did Felix play at the spring recital?
What did Felix ask to take home?

stories.text: After a heavy rainstorm, Hana heard a tiny meow coming from a drain pipe outside her flat. She tried to reach inside, but the pipe was too narrow for her arm. She called the fire station, and two firefighters arrived in a red van. Firefighter Dlamini used a long hose to gently push water through, and a soaked kitten slid out into Hana's hands. Hana dried the kitten with a towel and named her Puddle.
qs: Where was the meow coming from?
a drain pipe outside her flat
Why couldn't Hana reach the kitten?
the pipe was too narrow for her arm
What did Hana name the kitten?

stories.text: Every evening, old Mr. Aziz played chess with his grandson Sami on the balcony. For a whole year, Sami had never won a single game. One warm evening in June, Sami moved his knight and suddenly trapped his grandfather's king. Mr. Aziz stared at the board for a long time and then shook Sami's hand. He gave Sami his own wooden chess set, which he had carved as a young man.
qs: How long had Sami gone without winning?
What did Mr. Aziz give Sami?

stories.text: The parents of Greenfield School held a bake sale to raise money for new library books. Mrs. Nwosu brought chocolate brownies, and Mr. Petrov brought a tray of honey cake. By noon, everything was sold except a plate of very hard oatmeal biscuits. A little girl named Rosa bought them all to feed the ducks at the pond. The sale raised three hundred and forty pounds, enough for sixty new books.
qs: Why did the parents hold a bake sale?
to raise money for new library books
What was left unsold by noon?
a plate of very hard oatmeal biscuits
Why did Rosa buy the biscuits?
to feed the ducks at the pond
How much money did the sale raise?
